page: Amazon Web Services c8g.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is driven by a 64-bit ARMv9 processor utilizing AWS Neoverse-V2 cores operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. It provisions 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, assigning 1 execution thread per core. The processor features 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Memory allocation totals 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core.

The c8g.xlarge profile includes no integrated local storage and contains zero hardware accelerators or GPUs. Storage operations depend entirely on remote block storage solutions. The networking architecture delivers a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The ARMv9 instruction profile supports hardware AES acceleration but lacks x86-specific vector extensions such as AVX-512 or AMX, which affects specialized matrix and complex mathematical transformations.

Benchmark metrics demonstrate balanced multi-core throughput, logging 6817.37 in stress-ng multi-core testing and 5781.0 in multi-core Geekbench. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves strong performance at 14.25 GB/sec, placing it in the upper quartile of comparable systems. Large-block memory bandwidth sustains read rates of 96.22 GB/sec and write rates of 42.51 GB/sec. Conversely, synthetic encryption benchmarks and LLM token generation exhibit lower relative throughput, aligning with the architectural absence of dense vector pipelines and dedicated accelerator silicon.

The configuration is structurally suited for horizontally scalable compute tasks, including microservice APIs, static web serving with observed throughput of 9.92 GB/sec, CI/CD code compilation via Clang, and high-frequency in-memory key-value stores such as Redis.
description: Amazon Web Services c8g.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton ARMv9 architecture. It delivers 4 dedicated physical cores via Neoverse-V2 processors clocked at 2.8 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory at 2.0 GB per core. The configuration includes no local NVMe storage and provides no dedicated hardware GPUs, relying on external network-attached volumes alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate solid decompression capability, reaching top-quartile speeds in single-threaded bzip3 decompression, while general multi-core compute and memory bandwidth operate within expected mid-tier ranges. Cryptographic instruction tests and extended instruction sets reflect limited specialized hardware vector extensions. Designed for balanced compute workloads, the instance offers strong resource predictability due to dedicated non-threaded cores, making it suitable for distributed web serving, software compilation, batch processing, and caching tiers such as Redis.
